reconstructed_theorem_text: For every complete real inner-product normed additive commutative group E equipped with its compatible Borel measurable structure, every measure μ on E, and every function f : E → ℝ, assume that f is globally twice continuously Fréchet differentiable, f and its actual Hilbert gradient ∇f both belong to L²(μ), and x ↦ f(x)² log(f(x)²) is integrable with respect to μ. Here ∇ is the Hilbert Riesz inverse of the real Fréchet derivative, L² membership includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L² seminorm, and integrability includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the absolute value. Let S be the fixed Mathlib Real.smoothTransition and, for each n ∈ ℕ, define f_n(x) = S(2 − |‖x‖/(n+1)|) f(x), equivalently f_n(x) = radialSmoothCutoff(n+1, x) f(x). Then, as n tends to infinity through ℕ, all three limits hold: ∫_E f_n(x)² dμ(x) → ∫_E f(x)² dμ(x); ∫_E f_n(x)² log(f_n(x)²) dμ(x) → ∫_E f(x)² log(f(x)²) dμ(x); and ∫_E ‖∇f_n(x)‖² dμ(x) → ∫_E ‖∇f(x)‖² dμ(x). Every integral is a real Bochner integral and log is the totalized real logarithm with log(0) = 0. No finite-dimensionality, finiteness of μ, or probability normalization of μ is assumed.
objects: The ambient real Hilbert space E with its Borel measurable structure; a measure μ on E; the actual real-valued function f; its actual Hilbert gradient ∇f; the fixed smooth transition S = Mathlib Real.smoothTransition; and the locally defined functions f_n(x) = S(2 − |‖x‖/(n+1)|) f(x), with their actual Hilbert gradients ∇f_n. The three sequences are the squared-function integrals, the square-log integrals, and the squared-gradient-norm integrals of f_n.
domains: E is any type with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace ℝ, CompleteSpace, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures; finite-dimensionality is not required. μ is any Measure E, with no stated finite-measure or probability-measure requirement. f : E → ℝ; ∇f and ∇f_n : E → E; n ∈ ℕ; the radius n+1 is a positive real number. All integrands and integrals in the conclusion are real-valued. log is Real.log, including its value 0 at 0; convergence is in the usual topology of ℝ.
quantifiers: Universally quantify E and all displayed structures on it, then μ : Measure E and f : E → ℝ. The four hypotheses imply the conjunction of the three asserted limits. The sequence f_n is fixed by a let-definition, not existentially chosen or universally arbitrary. Each limit is indexed by n ∈ ℕ along atTop; x ∈ E is bound separately inside each integral. There is no quantified auxiliary constant or chosen subsequence.
assumptions: E has precisely the complete real inner-product normed additive group and compatible Borel structures displayed in the Lean type. The analytic hypotheses are ContDiff ℝ 2 f, MemLp f 2 μ, MemLp (gradient f) 2 μ, and Integrable (x ↦ f(x)² Real.log(f(x)²)) μ. MemLp means almost-everywhere strong measurability together with a finite L² seminorm; Integrable means almost-everywhere strong measurability together with a finite integral of the absolute value. ∇f is the literal Hilbert Riesz inverse of the Fréchet derivative, not an independently supplied field. No finite-dimensionality, compact-support assumption on f, restriction on the total mass of μ, or sign hypothesis on f is present.
conclusion: For the fixed f_n(x) = radialSmoothCutoff((n : ℝ)+1, x) f(x), the following three Tendsto assertions hold together: n ↦ ∫ f_n² dμ converges along atTop to ∫ f² dμ; n ↦ ∫ f_n² Real.log(f_n²) dμ converges along atTop to ∫ f² Real.log(f²) dμ; and n ↦ ∫ ‖gradient(f_n)‖² dμ converges along atTop to ∫ ‖gradient(f)‖² dμ. These are ordinary real integral limits, not merely almost-everywhere or pointwise convergence assertions.
scopes: μ and f are fixed throughout each instance of the implication and all three limits. The local family f_n is in scope for the entire conjunction. In gradient(f_n), the gradient is taken in the E variable x for the entire product x ↦ radialSmoothCutoff(n+1, x) f(x), with n held fixed. n tends to infinity through the natural numbers; there is no radius limit quantified independently of n. Each logarithm in this proposition is applied pointwise to the corresponding squared function, never to an integral. All integrals use the same μ. No hidden normalization of μ or quotient representative of f or its gradient is introduced.
constant_dependencies: There are no unspecified, existential, or estimated constants in the proposition. The exponent 2, the cutoff offset 2, the radius formula (n : ℝ)+1, and S = Real.smoothTransition are fixed parts of the statement, not choices depending on E, μ, or f. The limit values are exactly the corresponding integrals of the original f for the same E and μ; no rescaling, modified cutoff family, or additional parameter appears.
